A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIP/TVI research framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and the appendices report original representation-distance measurements, TVI–correctness correlations, and ablations across multiple models and datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds intervention, TVI-regularized training, automatic VIP detection, prompt-perturbation, and training-stage experiments.

M1.justification: v3 extends the diagnostic framework with TVI regularization during LLaVA instruction tuning, introducing a new training objective in Equation 5. Appendix B.2 replaces the coefficient-of-variation VIP detector with a variance-normalized rule using preceding layers, and Appendix E introduces weighted TVI. The original contrastive embeddings and default TVI remain.

E1.justification: The six main benchmarks and the CommonsenseQA/COCO control are retained. v3 adds instruction-tuning data from llava_v1_5_mix665k and tests image-only inputs and generic image-description instructions, modestly extending coverage within the existing vision-language domain.

E2.justification: The Visual Attention and Output Divergence comparators are unchanged in v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 3. New comparisons evaluate unregularized LLaVA against TVI-regularized training in v3 Table 5 and manual VIP selection against the revised automatic detector in Table 6.

E3.justification: v3 introduces inference-time PAI intervention, TVI-regularized training on a 60k subset, and evaluation of training checkpoints from 500 to 5000 steps. It also evaluates InstructBLIP and Qwen2.5-VL-32B/72B configurations. Existing benchmark splits, sample counts, temperature-zero generation, and agreement-based grouping are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test automatic versus manual VIP selection, intervention sensitivity, weighted versus uniform aggregation, instruction removal and prompt styles, training-stage evolution, and low-TVI correct-answer cases. These substantially expand validation beyond the retained distance-metric, model-scale, attention-map, and controlled-dataset analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 changes the statistical VIP estimator from a coefficient-of-variation cutoff to a group-mean difference normalized using group variances and sample sizes, with a historical-average threshold. Existing correlation p-values and dispersion reporting remain unchanged; no additional run counts, seeds, or repeated-run uncertainty are disclosed.

E6.justification: Original correlation tables and benchmark curves retain their values. Newly reported v3 comparisons include PAI accuracy of 50.00% versus 52.33% and TVI of 0.038 versus 0.144 (Table 2), and MME perception/reasoning scores of 1369.75/298.21 versus 1400.44/321.43 with TVI regularization (Table 5). Detector, aggregation, architecture, prompt, checkpoint, and failure-case results are also added.

T1.justification: Lemma F.2 removes the assertion that the distance is a strictly proper scoring rule and the corresponding proof argument, while retaining the Gaussian negative-log-density identity. The principal KL interpretation and H-divergence bounds remain. Appendix B.2 also revises the formal VIP-estimator definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: contrasting embedding chains reveals VIP, and post-VIP TVI quantifies language-prior reliance better than attention/output proxies. Updating the reported validation from nine models and 54 combinations to ten and 60 supplies broader supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains why correct answers can have low TVI and difficult questions can fail despite high TVI, adds a distribution-shift applicability caveat, and discusses limitations of image-only contrasts. It also interprets checkpoint stability as evidence for VIP's architectural/pretraining origins and discusses aggregation's accuracy–computation tradeoff. The earlier white-box limitation is retained and relocated.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the automatic detector's beta of 2.0, regularization weight of 0.03, and 60k training subset, and adds model architecture specifications and an InstructBLIP checkpoint reference. Existing preprocessing, decoding settings, and code-repository access remain unchanged. Last-token extraction was already documented in v1 Appendix C.

R1.justification: Appendix A's main research positioning is retained. New citations support last-token analysis, distribution-shift limitations, and multilingual/cultural applications. Everitt–Skrondal and Gneiting–Raftery are removed alongside the revised statistical and scoring-rule discussion. Consolidating the ViLP preprint/publication references does not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. Local rewrites clarify VIP selection and the density interpretation; headings, author naming, and the publication header change. Limitations move into the conclusion, while ethics and reproducibility statements move to the appendix. Scientific additions account for most expansion.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual reporting: intervention, training, detection, architecture, and aggregation tables, plus figures for automatic VIP selection, additional models, prompt perturbations, training trajectories, and failure cases. Existing plots are retained with resizing, repositioning, and expanded captions; the dataset table gains a group-ratio row.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better practical support through tested automatic VIP selection, intervention and training examples, and explicit robustness and failure analyses. These additions also clarify TVI's applicability limits. Their benefit is tempered by incomplete intervention setup reporting and inconsistent model layer counts between Tables 6 and 8, supporting a positive but limited overall improvement.
